body: Purpose: rebuild a business from its smallest operating unit (store, plant, branch, truck) and express each major cost in physical terms (people x wage, sq ft x rent, kWh x tariff), so the one or two micro-drivers that move margins before the P&L (wage notifications, tariff orders, related-party contracts) are named. Rule zero: write the edge question first (what consensus knows, which variable matters most, which layer reveals it); a method test gives no verdict (L9). Layers and time share for a 3-4 day dive: L1 map/peers 5%; L2 re-derived financials (leases, goodwill, ESOP, one-offs) 15%; L3 unit economics (revenue per unit and per sq ft, unit P&L, capex per unit, payback triangulated two ways) 20%; L4 cost lines >=3% of sales mapped to quantity x price with an external-input sensitivity in bps 20%; L5 governance, ownership and supply, incentives and strike prices, related-party table by year as share of each cost line (never skipped) 10%; L6 scuttlebutt with counts tied to model numbers 20%; L7 override table for good- and bad-looking flags 10%. Highest-yield Indian sources: annual-report notes (other expenses, Ind AS 24), BRSR (minimum-wage share, attrition, median pay), DRHP risk factors and KPIs, transcripts, broker analyst-meet notes, state wage gazettes. US: 10-K notes, DEF 14A, Form 4/144, BLS OES, FDD Item 19. Every estimate is tagged [EST], shows its method and a range, and stays unverified until a second route or a ground check agrees. Full text: research_notes/Deep dives/deep_dive_protocol.md.
